report_name: PEERSTITCH: Stealthy Implant Hits FortiGate via Chained CVEs

threat_actors.name: CL-STA-0954
threat_actors.description: A sophisticated threat cluster that targeted a telecommunications MSP by exploiting CVE-2024-47575 and CVE-2025-61624 to deploy the PEERSTITCH memory-resident malware.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor exploited CVE-2024-47575, a command injection vulnerability on an internet-facing FortiManager appliance, to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: The attackers exfiltrated a configuration archive (.tm file) from the compromised FortiManager device, which contained sensitive data for over 500 managed firewalls.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used legitimate credentials recovered from the exfiltrated FortiManager configuration archive to establish SSL/VPN sessions to perimeter firewalls.

attack_patterns.name: External Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used stolen credentials to access internal networks via FortiGate SSL/VPN services.

attack_patterns.name: Network Sniffing
attack_patterns.description: The attackers deployed unauthorized packet capture configurations on managed firewalls to map the network and intercept traffic.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
attack_patterns.description: A malicious `system.auto-script` object was used to execute shell commands as root to download and run the PEERSTITCH payload.

attack_patterns.name: Process Injection
attack_patterns.description: The PEERSTITCH malware patches the memory of legitimate FortiOS daemons, `sshd` and `httpslvpn`, to intercept and manipulate traffic.

attack_patterns.name: Modify Authentication Process
attack_patterns.description: PEERSTITCH patched the `sshd` daemon, allowing it to intercept or alter authentication flows through a legitimate process.

malware.name: PEERSTITCH
malware.description: A stealthy, memory-resident ARM64 implant designed for FortiGate appliances. It operates by patching legitimate system daemons like sshd and httpslvpn in memory to intercept traffic and evade detection, leaving no artifacts on disk.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2024-47575
vulnerabilities.description: A command injection vulnerability in FortiManager's management channel (TCP port 541) exploited for initial access, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to register a rogue virtual appliance and exfiltrate configuration data.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2025-61624
vulnerabilities.description: An authenticated path traversal vulnerability in the FortiOS auto-script engine exploited for privilege escalation to root, enabling the deployment of the PEERSTITCH implant.

identities.name: Telecommunications Managed Service Provider
identities.description: A telecommunications MSP was the primary target of the campaign, leading to the exposure of over 500 of its clients' firewalls.

identities.name: Fortinet
identities.description: Vendor of the FortiManager, FortiGate, and FortiOS products that were targeted and exploited in the campaign.

infrastructure.name: CL-STA-0954 Initial Compromise Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: IP address used by the attacker to exploit CVE-2024-47575 for initial access.

infrastructure.name: CL-STA-0954 Staging and C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: IP addresses used for staging, establishing SSL/VPN sessions, and hosting the PEERSTITCH payload for download.
